title: Highmoor Rising Revisited
premise: Ansel Blackwood, royal food-taster and secret charm-seller in the magic-outlawed city of Highmoor, discovers that the old gods are answering prayers again because someone is feeding them stolen souls — including his sister's, sold to the court beneath the mountain years ago. As dragon-fire, the last magic keeping the gods caged from mortal flesh, gutters toward extinction, Ansel must ally with a disgraced god-speaker and a turncoat palace guard to steal his sister's soul back. In the vault beneath the mountain he learns the queen herself brokered the soul-trade to buy her dynasty's survival, forcing him to choose between exposing the truth that will topple the throne and protecting the found family he's built in the palace kitchens. He chooses truth, returns his sister's soul to her body at the cost of his own immunity — and dies briefly, long enough for the old gods to claim him as their first honest servant in a century.
about_author: Lior Villalobos is a former line cook who claims the best plot ideas arrive during dinner rush, when the kitchen runs on superstition and small prayers. They write fantasy about people whose loyalties are tested by the institutions that feed them.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV: a routine morning tasting the queen's breakfast, then slipping charms to a desperate laundress after hours. He establishes his double life — trusted servant, outlaw peddler — and his careful neutrality. Emotional beat: the quiet exhaustion of belonging nowhere fully.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered Wrong
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV: a charm he sells actually works — violently, killing a man's debt-collector with root-growth through the lungs. The old gods haven't answered a prayer in a hundred years; now they're listening again. Ansel burns his stock, terrified. Emotional beat: dread dressed as guilt.

chapters.title: What the Kitchens Know
chapters.summary: Maren's POV (Ansel's fellow taster and closest friend): rumors ripple through the palace — the queen's dreams, missing servants, a sealed door beneath the mountain. Maren suspects Ansel of the sorcery stirring. Emotional beat: loyalty strained by suspicion.

chapters.title: The God-Speaker in the Wall
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV: he tracks the working to Sefa, a disgraced god-speaker living inside the city walls' hollow core. She tells him souls are being fed to the old gods to wake them — and shows him a ledger bearing his family name. His sister Wren's soul was sold seven years ago. Emotional beat: grief rekindled into purpose.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire Guttering
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV: she leads Ansel to the last dragon, chained beneath the palace as the realm's living seal on the gods' prison. Its flame is failing; when it dies, the gods walk free in flesh. The queen has been trading souls to delay it. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror at the cost of order.

chapters.title: The Turncoat
chapters.summary: Guard-captain Ivo's POV: blackmailed by the queen's spymaster, Ivo agrees to open the mountain road in exchange for his daughter's safety — but only if Ansel swears the theft won't touch the throne. Both men lie. Emotional beat: two compromised men recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV: the three descend through drowned mineshafts while Maren, suspicious, follows. They pass courts of the hungry dead who recognize Ansel's blood — Wren's bargain left a mark on him too. Emotional beat: claustrophobic intimacy; the team becomes a family under pressure.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Maren's POV: caught sneaking after them, Maren witnesses the soul-vault and the truth of the queen's bargains — and chooses to help rather than report. The vault keeper offers Ansel a trade: Wren's soul for his own years of immunity, the poison-tolerance that keeps him alive at court. Emotional beat: sacrifice made concrete and priced.

chapters.title: The Last Flame
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, climax: as the dragon-fire gutters out, the gods press against their weakening prison. Ansel pays the price, takes Wren's soul home, and publicly names the queen's crime before the court — choosing truth over the belonging he fought seven years to earn. The gods, honoring honesty, claim him as he collapses. Emotional beat: devastating triumph.

chapters.title: Highmoor Rising
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, resolution: waking in her own body after seven years, Wren navigates a changed city where magic is legal again and her brother lies between death and godhood. The old gods offer Ansel back — mortal, powerless, immune no more — and the found family of kitchen, wall, and guard take him in. Emotional beat: belonging finally chosen, not earned.
